questions: How do truth and authenticity differ, and why does reconstruction not by itself settle epistemic generation?

used_for: Two ways a recollection can be accurate

evidence.excerpt: In psychology, it is manifested in Ebbinghaus’s ([1885] 1913) foundational experimental work on memory for lists of nonsense syllables.

Adopting Bernecker’s (2010) terminology, authenticity refers to the correspondence between the memory representation and the subject’s experience of the past event, while truth refers to the correspondence between the memory representation and the past event itself.
Goldman 1999), and the problem of stored beliefs (Moon 2012).

sources.annotation: Distinguishes reconstructive remembering, truth, authenticity, and unresolved problems of epistemic preservation.
